A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Pages 2–8 and 12–16 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance; the remaining differences are fully inspectable.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-segmentation and image-classification experiments, ablations, and a six-volunteer user study in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including Tables 1–4, the user study, and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain identical LIT adaptation procedures, LoRA components, training losses, and prediction-validation steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same video-segmentation coverage on VOST, LVOSv2, MOSEv2, and SA-V, and image classification on CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, and SUN397. Human-study and supplementary scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SAM2.1, DAM4SAM, SAMURAI, CLIP, and the same alternative adaptation strategies in Tables 1–2, Figure 6, and the appendices.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, correction simulation, IoU thresholds, training budgets, metrics, and the six-participant user-study protocol are unchanged. The new hardware acknowledgement does not revise any stated experimental setting.

E4.justification: The epoch and adaptation-strategy ablations, adapter-location and correction-history analyses, predicted-IoU experiments, and qualitative success/failure cases are identical in Section 4.4 and Appendices B–D.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the 0.5 ± 0.2 s training-time report and plotted error bars. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, both Table 1 versions report 27.43 original versus 18.24 LIT corrections on VOST at IoU 0.5; appendix result tables and figures also match exactly.

T1.justification: The mathematical update rules, LoRA parameterization, and loss definitions in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: learning from corrections during inference, 18–34% fewer video-segmentation corrections, lightweight updates, and applicability across models and tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain identical, including the need for user monitoring, limitations of synthetic interactions, dependence on capable pretrained models, and explanations of failure cases in Appendices C–D.

D1.justification: v2 adds an acknowledgement of NVIDIA Academic Grant Program support using four RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. This is additional resource disclosure; the RTX Ada 6000 runtime specification, implementation details, hyperparameters, and project link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 66 references are retained with identical bibliographic text. Related-work discussion, novelty positioning, and relationships to earlier methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds one acknowledgement sentence and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgement shifts the bibliography across columns and pages 9–11. Figures, tables, captions, and the layout of the technical pages and appendices remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added NVIDIA funding/hardware acknowledgement provides limited additional disclosure. Methods, experimental evidence, claims, limitations, and all appendices are unchanged, while bibliography reflow has no substantive effect. There is no meaningful overall quality difference.
